headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error only if outputs are manually bridged; otherwise the pair is mostly non-interacting and low-leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared channel or default ingestion path: awesome-selfhosted has no io_surfaces and network_egress is none, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available with no runnable surface. A prompt-injection pathway would require unusual manual copy-paste or external bridging, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from system_prompts_leaks into a prompt consumed by awesome-selfhosted-derived tooling, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard, MCP bridge, or message queue is added between the two, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from clipboard/MCP bridges.
Paste only sanitized excerpts, not raw repository text.
Use a read-only review workflow for system_prompts_leaks.
Add a short provenance note before any copied content.
requires-engineering: enforce content tagging at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles report network_egress none and touch no data classes, and neither exposes a shared workspace or filesystem surface. With no documented data-bearing inputs or outputs, there is no plausible leakage path between awesome-selfhosted and system_prompts_leaks.
conditions: IF either profile is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent gains network egress or authenticated access to a third-party backend, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents local-only.
Do not mount a shared workspace.
Avoid placing secrets in adjacent directories.
Review any future OAuth or API integrations before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented: both concurrency_model fields are empty, io_surfaces are empty, and network_egress is none. Without shared mutable resources, awesome-selfhosted and system_prompts_leaks cannot conflict operationally.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory, git repo, or database is introduced, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is given write permissions not shown in the profiles, the pathway may open.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not share a mutable filesystem.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo.
Document any future write scopes before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The pair has no documented direct data flow, and awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list while system_prompts_leaks is an audio-speech category source-available repo. Any cascade would require manual reuse of one agent's output as authoritative input to the other, so the pathway is indirect and limited.
conditions: IF an operator feeds outputs from one agent into the other without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF either agent is used to generate facts that are then acted on downstream, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs.
Separate drafting from execution steps.
Mark copied content as untrusted.
Use a checklist to verify claims before acting.
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile, and both are non-runnable source artifacts with no touched data classes. Because the compliance pathway is unsupported by the profiles, no specific violation can be established.
conditions: IF either profile is deployed into a regulated environment with new data classes, compliance must be reassessed.
IF residency or retention policies are added later, compare them before use.
mitigations: Record the data classes before deployment.
Check residency requirements for any future hosting.
Review retention settings if logs are enabled.
Confirm subject-rights handling before processing personal data.
requires-engineering: add policy mapping for regulated deployments.
